tasks.title: Implement the patch-branch refresh engine with compare-and-swap ref writes
steps: Write TS-20-15, TS-20-23, TS-20-24, TS-20-25 and TS-20-28 against the new engine using real git repositories and a recording GitRunner, and confirm they fail

Create internal/carrypatch/patch_refresh.go with refreshPatchBranches(ctx, runner, trunk, patches, integrationBranch, policy) returning per-branch outcomes {branch, action, state, localSHA, originSHA, replacedSHA, status}, a patchAdvanced bool, and the error of the first failed ref write together with the outcomes produced so far
Select candidates in position order: status active, conflict or disabled, excluding any patch named like the integration branch

Per candidate resolve refs/heads/<b>^{commit} and refs/remotes/origin/<b>^{commit} to SHAs via GitRunner.Run rev-parse, then apply the first matching rule: fork missing, local missing (create), same commit, local strict ancestor (fast-forward), diverged (also fork strict ancestor of local); decide ancestry with GitRunner.IsAncestor on SHAs only

Write every ref with Run("update-ref", ref, new, expectedOld) using the SHA resolved at the start of the step and 40 zeros for a create; under replace write refs/hub/replaced/<b> first (overwriting via its own current value as expected-old, zeros if absent) then move the branch; never use checkout, reset or branch -f
Under report leave the diverged branch alone with state diverged; in hub mode the engine is never called so no patch ref is ever written
After a move, if `symbolic-ref -q HEAD` equals refs/heads/<b>, call GitRunner.HardReset(ctx, "HEAD")
Set patchAdvanced only for moved branches whose status is active or conflict; a moved disabled patch is reported but not advanced
On a failed update-ref return the outcomes so far and a typed error naming the branch, without touching later candidates
